leads.title: WSFS, F.S.B. v. Wahl, III and Brookside Properties, LLC (Confession of Judgment on $6M Commercial Guaranty Affirmed)
leads.why: Delaware Superior Court (Nov. 18, 2026) adopted a Commissioner's findings and affirmed that confession-of-judgment provisions in commercial guaranties signed by H. Adam Wahl, III and his company Brookside Properties, LLC are valid and enforceable, rejecting the guarantors' due-process waiver challenge after two evidentiary hearings. Brookside owned the commercial property (a fabrication shop) it leased to Quality Heating and Air-Conditioning, Inc., the $6,000,000 WSFS borrower that defaulted; Wahl and Brookside guaranteed the loan. Matters to CRE lenders and guarantors because it confirms Delaware courts will enforce confession-of-judgment clauses in commercial guaranties against both individual and LLC guarantors, letting a lender obtain judgment without a full merits trial.

leads.title: EPIC Companies Midwest, LLC v. HI West Acres, LLC (fka EPIC Hospitality) -- North Dakota bankruptcy adversary trial
leads.why: A jury trial began October 6, 2026 in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of North Dakota (Judge Peter Welte) in an adversary proceeding inside EPIC Companies Midwest's Chapter 11 case: EPIC Companies Midwest and EOLA Capital sued HI West Acres, LLC (formerly EPIC Hospitality, LLC) over roughly $900,000 tied to real estate development project financing.
